newsitem.title: SPAIN: Stet's Retevision bid helped by good Spain links.
newsitem.headline: Stet's Retevision bid helped by good Spain links.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday that the good relationship between Italy and Spain has helped Stet in its bid for Spain's second telephone operator Retevision, and that the results of the auction would be announced in a few days.

"In the coming days we'll have the results of this important auction. The result does not depend on the government at all, but the path of these talks has been helped by very good relations between the Spanish and the Italian governments," Prodi told reporters on a trip to Madrid for the NATO summit.

The competition for the 70 percent stake in state broadcaster Retevision is now between two consortiums: a group including Spanish electricity firm Endesa and Italy's Stet which have offered 180 billion pesetas for the stake; and the Opera group comprising Spanish bank BCH, France Telecom and U.S. operator Sprint which have presented an offer of 130 billion pesetas.
While Opera has been outbid financially, it said it could still win on other factors such as infrastructure and the future benefits for the Spanish economy.
After the presentation of offers on June 9, Spain's Development Minister Rafael Arias-Salgado said the winning bid could be announced at the end of June or the beginning of July.
But Retevision said that according to the conditions of the auction, a period of two months had been allotted to the evaluation of bids.
